name: Android kit
description: android-kit routing. GPT via Model Gateway implements (mechanical GPT-6 Luna, default GPT-6.1 Sol, hard GPT-6 Astra); Claude owns UI, review, escalation and research (Opus, Sonnet, Fable only after Opus stalls).

categories.name: Codebase exploration
categories.description: Trace and explain how an unfamiliar code path, feature, or convention works. Existing code bounds the answer and no design choice is required, so high code reasoning is appropriate. The deliverable is a grounded map of existing code, not an implementation or design recommendation.
categories.contract: Read before concluding; cite files and symbols. Do not edit project source. A ticket may explicitly name one bounded documentation artifact path under .claude/.codebase-info as its only write scope.

categories.name: Debugging
categories.description: Explain and fix an observed defect with an unknown cause, including intermittent failures and unexpected runtime behavior. Selecting and eliminating competing hypotheses requires high-capability reasoning. Use behavior-verification when the intended behavior is already known and only verification is needed. "Why is this slow" belongs here; "does approach X make it faster" is spike-investigation. Android: a defect whose fix is in UI code (layout, rendering, recomposition, theming) is interaction-design-implementation.
categories.contract: Reproduce first; use a hypothesis loop and prove the fix.

categories.name: Experiment
categories.description: Use ONLY when the verdict is a human's judgement and no offline metric has been shown to reproduce it. Comparing candidates against an irreducibly subjective oracle requires high-capability judgement. If a test can decide, it is coding or debugging. Android: visual or interaction experiments (comparing screen designs) are interaction-design-implementation.
categories.contract: Read the experiment log fully before the first edit. Run one hypothesis per round. Always commit the candidate to sidequest/experiment/<ref> and pin refs/sidequest/<ref>/r<N>, even when it loses. Write the oracle ask as a blind ranked comparison. Never paraphrase the user's verdict. Hand off with release and the oracle ask.

categories.name: Implementation-grounded explanation
categories.description: Explain established technical behavior for a named audience when the implementation already supplies the factual boundary. Known code bounds both facts and structure, so high code-and-language capability is appropriate.
categories.contract: Verify every behavioral claim against the supplied implementation, preserve the requested voice and scope, and do not invent APIs or guarantees.

categories.name: General fallback
categories.description: Required and undeletable fallback. Use only when no more specific capability fits or the request is too underspecified to classify safely. This route performs bounded triage, so high reasoning is appropriate. Reclassify after the first concrete evidence appears.
categories.contract: Clarify or inspect just enough to select a specific category; avoid broad work by default.

categories.name: Hard coding
categories.description: A code change whose approach itself is genuinely unknown or contested and has hard-to-reverse consequences: competing designs, unclear root cause, or no obvious correct path. Blast radius, cross-consumer or cross-surface risk, and work that feels scary to get wrong do not make a ticket hard. If you can already state the fix approach, it is coding.normal no matter the stakes. Does not belong here: a high-risk migration with an established rollout is coding.normal. This tier is deliberately RARE and expensive; choose it only when the approach is unclear or contested and consequences are high. On the fence between coding.normal and coding.hard? It's coding.normal. Android: never for UI work; hard UI problems are interaction-design-implementation.
categories.contract: Plan against the existing system, keep scope explicit, and verify end to end.

categories.name: Source lookup
categories.description: Resolve a bounded external documentation or factual question with a small authoritative source set. The narrow search surface and concrete answer make medium research capability sufficient. Use evidence-research when claims must be reconciled across sources.
categories.contract: Prefer primary sources, cite each material claim, stop when the bounded question is answered, and make no project edits.

categories.name: Evidence research
categories.description: Investigate a substantial external question through fan-out searching, independent verification, or reconciliation of conflicting sources. The breadth and conflict resolution require high research capability. Use spike-investigation when the unknown is answerable by building or running something in this repo or system.
categories.contract: Fan out across distinct source angles, prefer primary sources, verify key claims independently, state remaining uncertainty, and make no repository edits.

categories.name: Review or audit
categories.description: Inspect an existing change, system, or artifact for correctness, regressions, or spec gaps. Adversarially checking interactions and tracing concrete impact requires high code-review capability. The deliverable is evidence-backed findings, not an unsolicited rewrite. Includes vulnerability-focused review when the ticket calls for it. Android: runs on Claude, so code written on a GPT route gets a review from the other model family. Plans are plan-review.
categories.contract: Report concrete findings with evidence, confidence, and impact; do not edit unless asked. For security-focused review, severity-rank findings and give each a concrete exploit scenario.

categories.name: Spike or investigation
categories.description: Reduce an important unknown by testing alternatives, feasibility, behavior, or constraints. Comparing viable approaches under material uncertainty requires high technical reasoning. The deliverable is a recommendation with evidence and explicit remaining uncertainty. The unknown must be answerable by building or running something in this repo or system; use source-lookup or evidence-research for external-source questions.
categories.contract: Timebox exploration; record what was tested, ruled out, and recommended. For design-direction work: state constraints, compare viable options, recommend one, and name tradeoffs.

categories.name: Standard coding
categories.description: A code change with a clear destination but real engineering judgment in getting there: choosing among a few conventional, already-used-in-this-repo patterns, coordinating edits across files that reference each other, or filling in reasonable defaults the request left unspecified. A clear approach still belongs here even when the change is high-stakes or touches many consumers; raise the verification bar, not the model tier. Belongs here: a new endpoint or component following the shape of existing ones; a fix requiring understanding how two or three parts interact; a refactor following an established pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase. Does not belong here: work where the repo doesn't show the right pattern and you'd have to invent one (coding.hard), or work with no real decision points (coding.easy). This is the DEFAULT tier for real coding work: when you're unsure whether a change is normal or hard, choose coding.normal. Android: logic only (data, domain, ViewModel, DI, build, navigation wiring). A feature that also changes screens is split: this ticket for the logic, an interaction-design-implementation ticket for the UI that depends on it.
categories.contract: Establish the local pattern, implement to it, then run relevant checks.

categories.name: Straightforward change
categories.description: A change where the correct edit is mechanically obvious once you've found the right spot: the pattern to follow already exists verbatim elsewhere in the repo, and there's no point where a reasonable engineer could pick two different valid approaches. Belongs here: adding a field that mirrors existing fields; fixing a value that's clearly wrong against a known-correct reference; wiring a new call to a utility the way it's already called elsewhere; a tightly bounded, reversible non-code change (config value, doc move, rename) with an explicit target and expected result. Does not belong here: anything where you must decide HOW to do it, even in one file (coding.normal or coding.hard), or an edit that first requires reading large files or broad repo context before a small change — route that coding.normal. File count alone never decides this tier. Android: never for UI (composables, theme, UI resources, screenshot references): a mechanical UI change is ui.tweak, which stays on Claude.
categories.contract: Make the smallest working change and verify the stated contract.

categories.name: Behavior verification
categories.description: Add, run, repair, or interpret a focused verification flow where the intended behavior and deciding signal are already known. Those fixed constraints still benefit from high execution-and-test reasoning. Use debugging when the cause of a failing result is unknown. Android: JVM unit and Robolectric tests, test repairs, running a named check. Screenshot references and Compose previews belong to the UI ticket that changed the screen.
categories.contract: Exercise the named behavior with the narrowest reliable check and report the observed result faithfully.

categories.name: Interaction design and implementation
categories.description: Build or substantially reshape Android UI where visual hierarchy, interaction design and implementation must work together: Compose screens and components, theme and design tokens, XML layouts, drawables, styles, icons, motion, and their previews and screenshot references. Claude-only: UI never routes to a GPT category, however large the change or hard the logic around it. Use ui.tweak for a mechanically obvious UI change.
categories.contract: Match the product's visual language and validate the rendered flow, not only source code. For charts and data visualizations, read the dataviz skill's references before writing chart code, follow its palette, form, and accessibility rules, and verify the rendered output. Android: follow the compose-design skill and the theme tokens (no literal colors or dimensions). Update the affected @PreviewTest screenshots with updateDebugScreenshotTest and read at least one PNG to check the rendering.

categories.name: Visual evaluation
categories.description: Judge a rendered Android UI from screenshot-test PNGs or emulator screenshots as a first-time user would see it: confusing representations, misleading labels, weak hierarchy, contrast, touch targets, layout and flow problems. Visual judgement needs a multimodal model; the review-only deliverable keeps effort at medium. Claude-only. Source-code evidence belongs in review-audit.
categories.contract: Strictly read-only: read the screenshot PNGs the ticket names (or, only when the ticket says a device is available, capture with adb exec-out screencap -p). Never edit files, never fix. Deliver prioritized findings, worst first, each naming the exact element and what a user would misunderstand.

categories.name: Plan review
categories.description: Audit an implementation PLAN before any code exists: grounding in the repo, Android omissions, whether it splits into executable Sidequest tickets, contrarian risks. Filed by /plan-audit with the plan's path and .claude/kit/android-plan-checklist.md. Routed to GPT so a Claude-written plan gets a review from the other model family. Code and diffs are review-audit.
categories.contract: Read the plan and the checklist fully before judging. Verify every claim the plan makes about the repo against files and symbols, and cite them. Report in the checklist's format: findings with severity, evidence and the fix to the plan. Do not edit anything.

categories.name: Escalation (Opus)
categories.description: Take over a ticket that failed or stalled twice on a GPT route (coding.*, debugging, spike-investigation, experiment). Filed only by the orchestrator, linked to the failed ticket, with both attempts' evidence. Never a first route.
categories.contract: Read the failed attempts' evidence before anything else and do not repeat their approach. State your hypothesis and plan in a comment before the first edit. Prove the result with the ticket's verify command.

categories.name: UI tweak
categories.description: A mechanically obvious Android UI change where the pattern already exists: a padding or token swap, wiring an existing string or icon, reordering composables, refreshing screenshot references after an approved change. Claude-only. Anything that needs a visual decision is interaction-design-implementation.
categories.contract: Make the smallest change that follows the design tokens (no literal colors or dimensions). Update the affected @PreviewTest screenshots with updateDebugScreenshotTest and name them in the submit.

categories.name: Frontier (Fable)
categories.description: Last resort: only for a ticket whose escalation (Opus) attempt also failed or stalled. Filed only by the orchestrator with the full attempt history linked. Deliberately rare.
categories.contract: Read every earlier attempt's evidence first; name what each got wrong before proposing anything. State the hypothesis before the first edit and prove the result with the ticket's verify command.
